cic-cic:lever:4aba75cc-7ca0-4c59-b742-b6.title: Founder's Associate - Warsaw, PL
cic-cic:lever:4aba75cc-7ca0-4c59-b742-b6.description: Become the operational anchor and “second brain” to CIC’s Founder and Executive Chair. You will protect Tim’s time, preserve context, close loops, and help turn a remarkable range of relationships, ideas, and commitments into action. This is, at its core, an executive-assistance role - but one with unusually broad strategic and creative reach. You will own the calendar and inbox, masterplan complex international travel, keep important commitments from disappearing, research people and opportunities, steward senior relationships, and help operate Tim’s podcast and public communications. It shares much with a traditional Executive Assistant or Chief of Staff position, but with a broader connotation: a generalist working alongside Tim in his missions. Curiosity and experimentation matter more than arriving with a particular tool stack. ABOUT CIC CIC builds and connects thriving innovation communities around the world. Founded in 1999 in Cambridge, MA, we were one of the first companies to offer flexible office space and coworking. We manage a global network of innovation-focused workspace, laboratories, and event space across North America, Europe, and Asia, and continue to expand globally. ABOUT CIC WARSAW Opened in 2020, CIC Warsaw is one of the largest innovation-oriented centers in Europe. Our campus is located directly next to the Warsaw Central train station and is housed within Varso Place, a landmark on Warsaw’s map with the tallest building in the EU. Our Community and Relationship teams work closely to provide the best experience to our members. In addition, our Campus is also home to several global teams - including Finance, IT, Software, Recruitment, and Marketing—who support our global efforts. Learn more about us here. YOUR DAY-TO-DAY WORK As a Founder's Associate you will be responsible for protecting Tim's time, preserving context, closing loops, and helping turn a remarkable range of relationships, ideas, and commitments into action, while working closely with our Founder and Executive Chair. This is, at its core, an executive-assistance role - but one with unusually broad strategic and creative reach. It shares much with a traditional Executive Assistant or Chief of Staff position, but with a broader connotation: a generalist working alongside Tim in his missions. Potential responsibilities will include: Executive operations. Take end-to-end ownership of Tim's calendar and inbox—triaging, prioritizing, drafting and sending routine responses—and recommend what to accept, decline, delegate, shorten, combine, move or cancel. International travel. Plan complex, multi-country travel end to end, spot disruptions early, and redesign plans calmly when circumstances change. Continuity and decision support. Maintain a trusted system for commitments, decisions, priorities, and follow-ups; prepare concise briefings; research unfamiliar topics; and bring recommendations, not just information. Relationship stewardship. Help Tim stay meaningfully connected to senior colleagues, entrepreneurs, government leaders, diplomats, and partners around the world, including thoughtful outreach before trips. Podcast and media operations. Support Tim's podcast, Where Innovation Happens, including guest research, scheduling, publishing, subtitles, descriptions, clips, social promotion, and basic performance tracking. AI-forward ways of working. Use AI aggressively and thoughtfully: building durable institutional memory, automating routine work, improving research and communication, and continually redesigning inefficient processes. THE REQUIREMENTS - The "Systems Engineer": Proven track record of managing distributed infrastructure, network nodes, and bare-metal server architectures under real-world pressure. - Audit-Ready Discipline: Experience or familiarity handling ISMS audits and vulnerability tracking, keeping everything documented, clean, and airtight. - Hyper-Availability: This isn't a passive 9-to-5 desk role. Networks don't care about time zones, and outages must be crushed immediately. You must be available 7 days a week to act as our primary infrastructure responder. - Operational Autonomy: Completely self-motivated and highly organized; you can execute complex hardware or software purchasing pipelines and upgrade patches without losing track of a single asset or license. Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro. Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us. You will partner closely with GTM leadership across Japan to build high-quality pipelines for a wide range of roles. You will be expected to operate with urgency, precision and high judgment. You will not simply manage process. You will help shape markets, map talent, influence hiring strategy and close bar-raising candidates in highly competitive environments. WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT - You have helped build early GTM teams in new international markets. - You have recruited for frontier AI, developer tools, infrastructure, cloud or enterprise software companies. - You understand both commercial hiring and technical-adjacent GTM roles. - You have experience partnering with regional GMs, Sales VPs or founding country leaders. - You are comfortable moving between strategic talent mapping and hands-on execution. - You care deeply about quality, not just speed. - You know how to close candidates who have multiple options. thegialliancemanagementllccompany-thegia.description: Build a New Women’s Oncology Division in Phoenix The Specialty Alliance, is seeking a motivated Gynecologic Oncologist to help launch and lead a new women’s oncology division in the Greater Phoenix market. This is a unique opportunity for a physician who wants to do more than join an established practice — it’s a chance to help build something enduring within a growing, physician-led platform that already has a strong foundation in GI, GI infusion, Urology, and Radiation Oncology. We are looking for a physician leader who is excited about the opportunity to shape a growing oncology service line focused on women’s cancer. With strong operational support, marketing resources, referral development assistance, and transition support, this role is ideal for someone who wants long-term upside and the ability to influence clinical direction, growth strategy, and practice development from the ground up. Why This Opportunity Stands Out This opportunity is a strong fit for a physician who wants to help build and support a growing oncology division with Radiation Oncology support, while also benefiting from downstream revenue and long-term financial upside. Phoenix continues to offer strong growth potential, particularly in private practice oncology, and this model has the potential to be highly successful with the right physician leadership. We are committed to expanding the team with additional providers over time, including Medical Oncology, Gynecologic Oncology, and Breast Surgery support. The right candidate will have the opportunity to help shape a collaborative women’s cancer program with meaningful clinical and operational input. Practice Highlights Build a new gynecologic oncology division within an established physician-led platform. Work alongside Radiation Oncology support and broader oncology infrastructure. Help develop a women’s cancer program with long-term growth potential. Benefit from operational support, marketing, and referral relationship development. Join a platform with an existing presence in GI, GI infusion, Urology, and Radiation Oncology. Participate in a model with both clinical autonomy and long-term financial upside. Ideal Candidate Board-certified or board-eligible Gynecologic Oncologist. Entrepreneurial mindset with an interest in practice building. Strong clinical leadership and collaboration skills. Interest in working within a physician-led, multispecialty environment. Desire to help create a coordinated women’s cancer service line. Open to a role with growth, development, and long-term value creation. About Phoenix Phoenix continues to be one of the most attractive growth markets in the country, with a strong and expanding population base, robust referral potential, and a favorable environment for private practice specialty care. The metro area offers year-round sunshine, excellent schools, major universities, and a high quality of life for physicians and families. Compensation and Support Competitive compensation structure. Long-term financial upside tied to growth. Strong operational and marketing support. Assistance with transition logistics. Referral development support. Opportunity to be part of a growing, physician-led platform.
